title: Internet Connection Splitting: What's Old is New Again
problem: Systems with multiple network interfaces fail to fully utilize available bandwidth in parallel due to routing decisions that concentrate traffic on single paths. Modern data center topologies support multi-path forwarding but lack transparent splitting mechanisms.
motivation: As network interfaces proliferate and bandwidth becomes a critical bottleneck for data-intensive applications, better utilization of multiple paths can improve throughput and reduce congestion.
method: The system distributes data across multiple available network paths simultaneously, using classical load-balancing techniques that send entire conversations down one path or spread packets across all paths. It maintains packet ordering and respects network congestion. By applying these techniques transparently—without requiring applications to change—systems fully utilize the multi-path capabilities of modern data centers.
key_novelty: Transparent, automatic splitting of network connections across multiple paths, extending classical load-balancing to modern multi-path data centers.
contributions: Transparent traffic splitting across multiple network paths without application changes
Scheduling algorithm for distributing flows or packets across available connections
Improved bandwidth utilization and reduced latency in multi-path network topologies
limitations: Specific limitations not available from title alone; paper content required for detailed analysis.
